comparison: Perfect agreement on background claims (C1, C2, C8, C20, C114) about IgM evolution and conservation across vertebrates. Both treat these as established knowledge supporting the study's framework. Both evaluations: SUPPORTED.

Perfect agreement on infection model characterization (C39, C40, C47-C53). Both accept the viral infection model as methodologically sound and well-characterized through clinical observations, survival curves, qPCR, microscopy, and histology. Both evaluations: SUPPORTED.

Perfect agreement on protective immunity claims (C70-C75). Both accept the re-challenge experiments demonstrating protective immunity as valid evidence for IgM's functional role. Both evaluations: SUPPORTED.

Strong agreement on dual compartment IgM responses (C3, C41, C42, C63-C69). Both acknowledge solid evidence for IgM responses in systemic and mucosal compartments. Peer review explicitly praises 'dual role' demonstration. OpenEval also includes C62 from transcriptomic data. Both evaluations: SUPPORTED.

Strong agreement on IgM depletion experiments (C4, C43, C78-C81). Both accept that IgM depletion leads to increased viral loads, pathology, and mortality. OpenEval notes potential off-target effects as caveat; peer review acknowledges variability but treats findings as key strength. Both evaluations: SUPPORTED.

Partial overlap on depletion model characterization (C76-C77). OpenEval separately evaluates the depletion model validation as SUPPORTED. Peer review incorporates these claims into broader assessment of depletion experiment outcomes (R2). Both accept the methodology.

Strong agreement on transcriptomic and immune response characterization (C54-C61, C94). Both accept gene expression analysis and temporal dynamics of immune responses. OpenEval includes additional claims (C62, C92, C93) about viral load distribution. Both evaluations: SUPPORTED.

Agreement on neutralization capacity (C44, C82-C86). Both accept in vitro neutralization assays as valid evidence. Peer review also includes mechanistic claims (C6, C87-C89, C111) in same evaluation, while OpenEval separates these into R13. Both evaluations: SUPPORTED.

Agreement on neutralization mechanism (C6, C87-C89). OpenEval separately evaluates time-of-addition assay data showing IgM acts on viral particles before cell entry. Peer review groups these mechanistic claims with broader neutralization findings. Both evaluations: SUPPORTED.

Divergent evaluations on major conclusions (C5, C107-C108). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with caveats about incomplete characterization of IgM vs IgT contributions. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, noting concerns about 'overstatement of findings' novelty' and presentation strength relative to existing literature.

Divergent evaluations on evolutionary conservation claims (C7, C46, C112). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting speculation about 'conserved principles' and lack of direct comparative experiments. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED, explicitly accepting that 'IgM's role has been conserved across jawed vertebrates for over 500 million years.'

OpenEval separately evaluates background claims on immunoglobulin evolution (C9-C19) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; these background claims were not specifically addressed by reviewers.
